gaps.title: r_multiple scale 4 (legacy) vs 8 (modern)
gaps.closure_criteria: Scale decision recorded + migration mapping
gaps.closure_note: CLOSED 2026-10-04 (Phase 4). The storage side was already decided (ADR-001 §3: numeric(20,8), 'storing at higher precision than display never loses parity'); what was missing was the COMPARISON rule, now in packages/domain/src/legacyParity.ts: imported values are preserved BY VALUE (the column normalises '1.6450' -> 1.64500000 and nothing rounds them again), and a historical recomputation is compared at the legacy scale (4) with the legacy rounding mode (bcmath-truncate). The mode is load-bearing: 1.000099999 truncates to '1.0000' but half-even rounds to '1.0001', so a recomputation using the modern default would fail ~1 in 10,000 non-terminating quotients. Truncation is toward zero and idempotent (the migration's own property). Verified by 8 unit tests and by the load rehearsal's gate 6, which recomputed 5 migrated trades with the production computePnl and matched both net PnL and R at scale 4.
